definition: Producing a pixel-level mask separating an object from the background — the generic term behind instance and semantic segmentation.
details: Producing a pixel-level mask separating an object from the background — the generic term behind instance and semantic segmentation.

explainer.lead: Object segmentation produces a pixel-level mask that separates an object from the background. It matters as the generic term behind instance and semantic segmentation.

tiers.eli5: Instead of drawing a box, it colours in every pixel that belongs to the object, like a careful cut-out.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers train models to output per-pixel masks for the object; a common pitfall is that mask quality drops at object boundaries and for thin structures.
tiers.paperLevel: A model maps each pixel of an image to a mask value separating object from background; it underlies instance and semantic segmentation, and boundary accuracy is a known limit.

explainer.example: A portrait is processed and every pixel of the person is marked, leaving the background unmarked.
